raw.details:
India Got Spot 1.0 is an offline hackathon organized by Swastik Community, designed to bring together passionate developers, creative thinkers, aspiring entrepreneurs, designers, and technology enthusiasts to develop innovative solutions to real-world problems.

The hackathon provides a platform for students and aspiring innovators to transform their ideas into practical technology-driven solutions. Participants will get an opportunity to demonstrate their technical knowledge, creativity, problem-solving abilities, teamwork, and capacity to build meaningful projects within a time-bound environment.

In a world where technology continues to reshape industries, businesses, and everyday life, India Got Spot 1.0 aims to encourage participants to think beyond conventional approaches and explore new possibilities through innovation. Whether it is developing an AI-powered application, building a modern web platform, creating a FinTech solution, experimenting with Web3 technologies, or contributing to open-source innovation, participants are encouraged to develop solutions that address genuine challenges.

The event will begin with participant reporting and orientation at 8:00 AM on 15 February 2027 and conclude at 8:00 PM on the same day. Within this 12-hour event window, participants will work on their projects, demonstrate their progress, present their solutions, and compete for recognition and a total prize pool of ₹30,000.

India Got Spot 1.0 is not just about building software. It is about developing a problem-solving mindset, learning through collaboration, exploring emerging technologies, and turning promising ideas into impactful solutions.

Vision and Mission:

  • The vision of India Got Spot 1.0 is to create an innovation-driven environment where emerging talent can explore technology, develop practical solutions, and gain valuable experience beyond traditional classroom learning.
  • The mission is to encourage young innovators to identify real-world challenges, experiment with modern technologies, collaborate with like-minded individuals, and build solutions that have the potential to create meaningful impact.
  • Through this initiative, Swastik Community aims to promote innovation, technical learning, collaboration, and a strong problem-solving culture among students and aspiring developers.

Objectives of the Hackathon

  • Encourage innovation: Motivate participants to develop original ideas and creative approaches to existing problems.

  • Promote practical learning: Provide a time-bound environment in which participants can apply their technical knowledge to real-world challenges.

  • Explore emerging technologies: Encourage experimentation with AI, web development, FinTech, Web3, open-source technologies, and other relevant fields.

  • Develop teamwork: Strengthen communication, collaboration, planning, and execution skills.

  • Build problem-solving abilities: Help participants understand how to identify problems, design solutions, and implement working prototypes.

  • Support young talent: Provide students and aspiring innovators with an opportunity to showcase their capabilities.

  • Recognize excellence: Reward outstanding solutions through evaluation, recognition, and the event's ₹30,000 total prize pool.

Hackathon Domains

  • Participants can propose and develop projects across the following domains.

Artificial Intelligence (AI)

  • Explore AI-powered solutions that automate processes, improve decision-making, enhance productivity, and solve practical problems. Potential areas include intelligent assistants, predictive analytics, machine learning applications, AI-powered education tools, cybersecurity, and responsible AI systems.

Web Technologies

  • Build modern, responsive, and user-friendly web applications that improve digital experiences. Ideas may include productivity platforms, educational portals, community applications, business tools, accessibility solutions, and full-stack web products.

Financial Technology (FinTech)

  • Develop technology-driven solutions that improve financial accessibility, transparency, financial literacy, payments, budgeting, expense management, or other financial processes.

Web3 and Blockchain

  • Explore decentralized technologies, blockchain-based applications, digital identity, transparent systems, smart contracts, and other relevant use cases where decentralized architecture offers meaningful benefits.

Open Source

  • Create tools, applications, developer utilities, or community-oriented projects that encourage collaboration, transparency, accessibility, and reusable technology.

Emerging Technologies and Open Innovation

  • Participants may also propose ideas involving other emerging technologies or interdisciplinary approaches, provided their projects address a clear problem and demonstrate meaningful technical innovation.
  • These domains are intended to encourage exploration. The quality, feasibility, originality, and potential impact of a solution will be more important than simply choosing a particular technology.

Participation and First-Round Selection

  • India Got Spot 1.0 will follow an initial project idea submission round, followed by shortlisting for the offline hackathon.

Round 1: Project Idea Submission:

  • Participants will submit a PowerPoint presentation explaining their proposed project. The presentation should clearly communicate the problem, the intended solution, its target users, the proposed technology stack, and the expected impact.

The PPT should include:

  1. Project title and a brief introduction.

  2. Problem statement and the issue being addressed.

  3. Proposed solution and its key features.

  4. Target audience or intended beneficiaries.

  5. Proposed technology stack and implementation approach.

  6. Innovation, uniqueness, and potential impact.

  7. A basic development plan or prototype concept.

Participants should focus on clarity, feasibility, originality, and the value their idea can deliver. A well-defined problem and a practical solution are preferable to an unnecessarily complicated concept.

Shortlisting Process

  • Submitted ideas will be reviewed according to the announced evaluation criteria. Projects demonstrating a clear problem statement, a feasible implementation plan, originality, technical relevance, and meaningful potential impact may be shortlisted.
  • Shortlisted participants will receive the relevant instructions regarding confirmation, reporting, team arrangements, and event participation.
  • The submission deadline, shortlisting announcement, team-size rules, and final submission instructions will be communicated through the official event channels.

The 12-Hour Offline Building Experience

  • The main hackathon will take place on 15 February 2027, from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
  • During the event, shortlisted participants will work on their proposed projects, refine their concepts, develop functional prototypes, and prepare their final demonstrations.
  • The 12-hour format encourages participants to manage time effectively, prioritize essential features, collaborate efficiently, and focus on building a solution that demonstrates its core purpose.
  • Participants are encouraged to develop working prototypes rather than relying exclusively on presentations. Depending on their project, a demonstration may include a functioning web application, an AI-powered workflow, a technical prototype, a blockchain-based implementation, or another suitable proof of concept.
  • The emphasis will be on demonstrating the project's core functionality, explaining technical decisions, communicating its practical value, and showing how it addresses the identified problem.

Project Development and Deliverables

Participants should aim to complete a meaningful prototype within the available development window. Projects should demonstrate a clear connection between the identified problem and the proposed solution.

Depending on the nature of the project, expected deliverables may include:

  • A working prototype or minimum viable product (MVP).

  • A project presentation explaining the problem and solution.

  • A clear demonstration of the major features.

  • A description of the technology stack and implementation approach.

  • A repository or relevant project files, where applicable.

  • A brief explanation of future improvements and scalability.

Participants should ensure that their projects are presented honestly. Any third-party APIs, datasets, open-source libraries, AI tools, or external services used should be acknowledged where appropriate.

A polished prototype is valuable, but a project will also be assessed on its problem-solving approach, technical reasoning, originality, and potential usefulness.

Judging Criteria

  • Projects may be evaluated across the following proposed parameters:
  • Innovation and Originality: The uniqueness of the idea and how creatively it approaches the identified problem.
  • Problem Relevance: How clearly the project identifies a genuine problem and addresses the needs of its intended users.
  • Technical Implementation: The quality of the implementation, appropriate use of technology, and demonstrated functionality.
  • Feasibility and Practicality: Whether the proposed solution can realistically be developed, used, and improved.
  • User Experience and Design: The usability, accessibility, interface clarity, and overall quality of the solution.
  • Impact and Scalability: The project's potential to benefit users and grow beyond the initial prototype.
  • Presentation and Demonstration: The clarity of the final explanation, demonstration, and responses to evaluators' questions.
  • The final evaluation framework, parameter weightings, and scoring methodology will be communicated by the organizing team before or during the event.

Prize Pool and Recognition

  • India Got Spot 1.0 features a total prize pool of ₹30,000, intended to recognize outstanding innovation, technical execution, and problem-solving.
  • The prize distribution, award categories, eligibility requirements, and any additional recognition will be announced through the official event communication channels.
  • Participants should note that the stated amount represents the total prize pool, not an individual guaranteed award. Final awards will be determined according to the official rules and judging process.
  • Beyond prizes, the hackathon offers participants an opportunity to strengthen their portfolios, gain practical development experience, learn from other builders, and showcase their work in a competitive environment.

Who Should Participate?

India Got Spot 1.0 is intended for students, aspiring developers, designers, technology enthusiasts, innovators, and individuals interested in building technology-driven solutions.

It is suitable for participants who want to:

  • Transform an idea into a working prototype.

  • Explore new technologies and practical applications.

  • Collaborate with other motivated builders.

  • Improve their technical and presentation skills.

  • Experience a structured, time-bound hackathon.

  • Demonstrate their abilities through a real project.

Participants should review the official eligibility and team-formation rules before submitting their ideas.

Participant Guidelines

To maintain a fair, productive, and collaborative environment, participants are expected to follow the official event rules.

  1. Submit original project ideas and respect the intellectual property of others.

  2. Provide accurate information during registration and submission.

  3. Follow the announced deadlines, reporting instructions, and submission requirements.

  4. Use third-party resources, datasets, and tools responsibly and in accordance with their applicable terms.

  5. Clearly identify the work completed during the hackathon and acknowledge relevant external contributions.

  6. Maintain professional conduct and respect other participants, mentors, judges, and organizers.

  7. Ensure that the final project can be explained and demonstrated by the participating team.

  8. Follow the organizers' instructions regarding venue access, safety, equipment, and event logistics.

Any additional rules regarding team size, pre-existing projects, AI-assisted development, intellectual property, and disqualification will be specified in the official guidelines.

Why India Got Spot 1.0?

India Got Spot 1.0 provides an opportunity to move beyond theoretical knowledge and experience the process of building under real time constraints.

The hackathon encourages participants to think critically, make informed technical decisions, work collaboratively, and focus on solutions that can deliver practical value. It creates space for experimentation, learning, and the exchange of ideas among individuals who share an interest in technology and innovation.

For beginners, it can be a chance to take the first step toward building a real product. For experienced developers, it can be an opportunity to test their skills, experiment with new technologies, and refine their ability to deliver under pressure.

Every project represents an opportunity to learn something new, whether through successful implementation, technical challenges, collaboration, or feedback received during evaluation.

About the Organizer: Swastik Community

Swastik Community is the organizing community behind India Got Spot 1.0, with a focus on encouraging technology, innovation, collaboration, and opportunities for emerging talent.

Through initiatives such as hackathons and technology-focused events, the community aims to create an environment where students and aspiring innovators can connect, share ideas, develop practical skills, and explore meaningful projects.

India Got Spot 1.0 reflects this objective by bringing project-based learning and competitive innovation together in a focused, one-day offline experience.

Important Event Information

  • Event Name: India Got Spot 1.0

  • Organizer: Swastik Community

  • Date: 15 February 2027

  • Reporting and Start Time: 8:00 AM

  • Scheduled Conclusion: 8:00 PM on the same day

  • Format: Offline hackathon

  • Duration: 12 hours

  • Venue: To Be Announced

  • Total Prize Pool: ₹30,000

  • Selection Process: PPT-based project idea submission followed by shortlisting

  • Domains: AI, Web Technologies, FinTech, Web3, Open Source, and Emerging Technologies

The venue, submission deadlines, shortlisting details, team rules, prize distribution, and other operational information will be announced through official event communications.

Join the Innovation Journey

  • India Got Spot 1.0 invites aspiring builders to bring forward their ideas, challenge conventional thinking, and work toward solutions that address meaningful problems.
  • Whether your interest lies in artificial intelligence, web development, financial technology, decentralized systems, open-source innovation, or another emerging field, this hackathon offers a focused environment to explore your potential and demonstrate what you can build.
  • Prepare your idea, explain the problem you want to solve, develop a practical approach, and get ready to turn your vision into a working prototype.
